title: Where is it? Places and buildings (Wo?)
summary: Say where something is: im Büro, am Bahnhof, auf dem Tisch, neben der Tür. Ask Wo? and Wohin?, and find your way around a building.
goals: Say where something is with in, an, auf, neben, hinter, vor, zwischen + dative
Find your way in a building: im ersten Stock, der Aufzug, die Treppe

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 9: Working life (Wo ist der Aufzug?)
Nicos Weg A1, chapter 10: Orientation (Im Büro)

sections.title: Wo? + dative
sections.text:
To say **where** something is, use [[in]], [[an]], [[auf]], [[neben]], [[hinter]], [[vor]] or [[zwischen]] + the dative:
- [[Der Laptop ist auf dem Tisch.]] (on)
- [[Die Lampe ist neben dem Fenster.]] (next to)
- [[Ich bin im Büro.]] ([[im]] = [[in dem]])
- [[Ich warte am Bahnhof.]] ([[am]] = [[an dem]]: at the station)
- [[Die Toilette ist hinter der Tür.]]

sections.title: Wo? or Wohin?
sections.text:
**Wo?** asks where something is. **Wohin?** asks where it's going:
- [[Wo bist du?]] - [[Im Büro.]]
- [[Wohin fährst du?]] - [[Nach Hause.]] / [[Zum Bahnhof.]] / [[Nach Salzburg.]]

Answers with [[zu]] and [[nach]] are dative too, so they work now. With [[in]] or [[an]], a movement takes the accusative: [[ins Kino]] (Unit 3; [[ins]] = [[in das]]), [[in die Stadt]]. That comes properly at A2.

Russian makes the same split: где? (Wo?) and куда? (Wohin?), with a different case for each: в офисе (where), в офис (where to). German does it with [[in]] too: [[im Büro]] (Wo?), [[ins Büro]] (Wohin?, A2).

sections.title: In a building
sections.text:
- [[im Erdgeschoss]] = on the ground floor
- [[im ersten Stock]] = on the first floor (one floor up, as in British English; American 'second floor')
- [[oben]] = upstairs, [[unten]] = downstairs
- [[der Aufzug]] = the lift, [[die Treppe]] = the stairs
- [[der Eingang]] and [[der Ausgang]] = the entrance and the exit
- [[Wo ist die Toilette?]] - [[Im zweiten Stock, links.]]

[[im ersten Stock]] works like [[am dritten Mai]]: the ordinal gets -en after [[dem]].
[[hier]] = here, [[da]] = there (or here), [[dort]] = over there: [[Der Aufzug ist dort, neben der Treppe.]]

items.de: Wo ist der Aufzug? - Dort, neben der Treppe.
items.en: Where's the lift? - Over there, next to the stairs.

items.de: Das Büro ist im dritten Stock.
items.en: The office is on the third floor.

items.de: Mein Handy ist auf dem Tisch.
items.en: My phone is on the table.

items.de: Der Drucker ist zwischen dem Fenster und der Tür.
items.en: The printer is between the window and the door.
I'm waiting in front of the entrance.
Where are you going? - To the supermarket.
On the second floor, on the left.

items.de: Der Schlüssel ist auf dem Tisch.
items.en: The key is on the table.
I'm waiting in front of the entrance.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: The key is on the table.
items.explanation: Wo? + dative: der Tisch becomes dem Tisch.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap with one word (a short form): I'm in the office.
Fill in the gap: The toilet is next to the kitchen.
items.explanation: die Küche is feminine: in the dative, die becomes der.

items.question: Which question asks where someone is going?
items.explanation: wohin = where to; wo = where; woher = where from.

items.question: Which one means 'on the first floor'?
items.explanation: in dem ersten Stock: im, and the ordinal gets -en after dem.
